edition_notes: Pressman Toy Corporation, ©2009, code 4418/0710; 2 to 4 players, ages 8 to adult

items.rule: Place all Tri-Omino tiles face down and mix them; they form the pool, and the tiles left after dealing form the 'well'.
A scorekeeper writes down each player's name on paper and adds or subtracts points in each player's column as plays are made.
In a 2-player game each player takes 9 tiles.
In a 3- or 4-player game each player takes 7 tiles.
Players place their tiles on their rack with the numbers facing themselves and must hide them from the other players.
The round starts with the player holding the triple tile (three identical numbers) of the highest value (5-5-5 is highest, then 4-4-4, etc.), who places it face up on the table.
The starting player scores the sum of the three numbers on the starting tile plus a 10 point bonus.
If the three 0s tile starts the round, the player gets a 30 point bonus in addition to the normal 10 point bonus (plus the tile sum of 0).

A player holding both the highest triple and the three 0s may start with either; to start with the three 0s for the bonus, they must show the other players the tile with the highest same-number triple.
If no player has a triple tile, the player with the highest total on one tile starts and scores that total with no bonus points.

Play proceeds clockwise; on a turn the player must try to match two numbers (a side) of a tile already on the table with one of their tiles, and scores the sum of the three numbers on the tile placed.
A player who cannot match draws tiles from the well, keeping them separate from the hand until a matching tile is picked.
For each tile drawn from the well, 5 points are deducted from the player's score; after the deduction, the points of the matching tile played are added.
If a player cannot match and the well is empty, 10 points are deducted from their score and play continues.
Closed hexagon bonus: matching all three numbers of a tile and forming a closed hexagon scores the sum of the three numbers plus 50 points.
Bridge bonus: matching a tile by one side and the point opposite forms a bridge and scores the sum of the three numbers plus 40 points.
After a bridge has been formed, a player who matches two sides of a tile (completing it) receives the sum of the three numbers plus a 40 point bonus.
A round ends when a player plays all their tiles, or when all players have passed and the game is blocked.
The player who plays all their tiles first wins the round and gets a 25 point bonus plus the total points of all tiles left in the other players' hands; the others do not deduct those points.
If the game is blocked, the player with the fewest tiles wins the round and adds all points from the other players' hands, with no bonus points.
In a blocked round, the winning player must also deduct the total points left in their own hand from their score.
For a new round, turn all tiles face down, mix them, and each player picks new tiles; the round starts as the first, with the player who now holds the highest triple.
The game ends when a player reaches 400 points; if this happens mid-round, play continues until the round is over.
The first player to reach 400 points wins the game.
If more than one player passes 400 points during the round, the winner of that round wins the game.
